definitions.explanation: The Japanese punctuation mark (・) placed at the center of the line, used to separate items in a list, mark boundaries in katakana words, or indicate an abbreviation.

examples.japanese: {中黒|なかぐろ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{区切|くぎ}る→区切る：11850_kugiru⟧。
カタカナ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人名|じんめい}→人名：22206_jinmei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{中黒|なかぐろ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{姓|せい}→姓：15390_sei⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{名|めい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{分|わ}ける→分ける：02333_wakeru⟧。
examples.english: In katakana names, an interpunct separates the surname and given name.

examples.japanese: ⟦{並列|へいれつ}→並列：08417_heiretsu⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{列挙|れっきょ}→列挙：11777_rekkyo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧とき、⟦{読点|とうてん}→読点：16992_touten⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{代|か}わり→代わり：01296_kawari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{中黒|なかぐろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: When listing parallel terms, an interpunct is sometimes used instead of a comma.

notes:
Also called {中点|なかてん} or {中ポツ|なかぽつ}. The character ⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧ means "middle" and {黒|ぐろ} means "black (dot)," describing its appearance as a dot positioned in the middle of the line.

USAGE:
The {中黒|なかぐろ} (・) serves several functions in Japanese writing:
- Separating items in a list: ⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧・⟦{青|あお}→青：02841_ao⟧・⟦{黄|き}→黄：19352_ki⟧
- Marking word boundaries in katakana: マイケル・ジャクソン
- Separating parallel or contrasting items: {和|わ}・⟦{洋|よう}→洋：28890_you⟧
- Indicating date components: 2024・3・15

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {中黒|なかぐろ}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{区切|くぎ}る→区切る：11850_kugiru⟧ — to separate with an interpunct
- {中黒|なかぐろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧ — to type/insert an interpunct
- {中黒|なかぐろ}⟦{区切|くぎ}り→区切り：21082_kugiri⟧ — interpunct-delimited

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{読点|とうてん}→読点：16992_touten⟧ — comma (、); the standard Japanese comma
- ⟦{句点|くてん}→句点：19157_kuten⟧ — period (。); the Japanese full stop
- {中点|なかてん} — interpunct; an alternative name for the same mark
